items.title: Tanker attacked off Saudi Arabia as Gulf shipping attacks rise
items.why: UKMTO, the UK maritime security agency, says a tanker was struck about 68 nautical miles north-east of Jubail, Saudi Arabia, on Friday; the crew were safe. BBC Verify counted 12 ships attacked around the Strait of Hormuz on 5–11 October, the most in any week of the war.
items.matters: Oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz have slowed as attacks spread, according to shipping data cited by BBC Verify.

items.title: Tamil film composer Deva, known for Rajinikanth theme music, dies at 75
items.why: Deva, who composed music for more than 400 films in Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam, died in Chennai, India, on 17 October after being taken to hospital, reports say. Known as 'Thenisai Thendral', he brought Chennai's gaana street music into mainstream Tamil cinema.
items.matters: His title-card theme from Annamalai (1992) is still used to open Rajinikanth's films.

items.title: US tech shares have worst week since June on AI spending doubts
items.why: The Nasdaq fell 2.1% on Friday 16 October and 4.5% over the week, its worst week since June, as chipmakers and AI companies slid. Cloud firm CoreWeave, which carries about $50 billion of debt, fell around 12% on the day and nearly 25% over the week.
items.matters: Bets on higher US interest rates make borrowing dearer for debt-funded AI data-centre builders, adding to doubts about the AI boom.

items.title: US measles cases pass 4,400 this year, nearly double last year's total
items.why: The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported 4,410 confirmed measles cases this year as of 15 October, up 330 in a week, with 451 hospitalisations. Pennsylvania, the hardest-hit state, reports five measles-related deaths. Last year's total was 2,289.
items.matters: The US and Mexico are due to meet the Pan American Health Organization next month to review their measles elimination status.

items.title: FIFA fines Spain's federation over anti-Muslim chants at Egypt friendly
items.why: FIFA has fined the Spanish football federation $20,000 and ordered at least 15% of seats closed at Spain's next home friendly, after fans chanted against Muslims during a 0-0 draw with Egypt near Barcelona on 31 March. Reuters reports the federation will appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport.
items.matters: FIFA rejected Spain's argument that the word "Muslim" was not insulting, ruling that context can make it discriminatory.

items.title: Ethiopia names a six-month interim government for Tigray
items.why: Ethiopia's Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed on Friday named a federal caretaker administration to run the northern Tigray region for six months, promising elections afterwards. It follows an offensive by the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) in September; Reuters reports federal forces have since taken the regional capital, Mekelle.
items.matters: Tigray was the scene of a 2020–22 war between federal forces and the TPLF, which once ran the region.

items.title: Bangladesh dengue deaths reach 335 this year as cases pass 108,000
items.why: Bangladesh's health directorate reported four more dengue deaths on 16 October, bringing this year's toll to 335, with 108,440 cases recorded. September was the deadliest month so far, with 148 deaths, and infections are continuing past the usual June-to-September season.
items.matters: Dengue, spread by mosquitoes, has no specific treatment; Bangladesh's government has ordered neighbourhood awareness campaigns to curb it.

items.changed: Updated: Trudy weakened to Category 1 but will pass close to the coast tonight
items.title: Hurricane Trudy weakens but nears Mexico's Pacific coast with flood risk
items.why: Hurricane Trudy weakened to Category 1 on Friday but was nearing Mexico's Pacific coast on Saturday with winds near 150 km/h, the US National Hurricane Center says. It should pass close to Colima and Jalisco tonight; Mexico's weather service expects it to stay offshore. No deaths have been reported.
items.matters: Up to 38 cm of rain could fall on ground already soaked by earlier storms, raising the risk of floods and landslides.

items.title: Indian police detain 'Cockroach' protest founder ahead of New Delhi rally
items.why: Police in New Delhi detained the founder of the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party, on Friday before a planned flag march, and say about 150 people were held. Protesters want the chief election commissioner to resign over a voter-roll revision that removed more than 130 million names.
items.matters: In the world's largest democracy, critics say the revision favours Prime Minister Modi's BJP; the Election Commission denies favouring any party.

items.title: Astronomers identify the first known green star, tinted by swallowed planet debris
items.why: University of Warwick astronomers say WD J1330+6435, a white dwarf about 280 light-years away in the constellation Draco, would look green to the human eye. Sodium from rocky debris of its former planets absorbs orange and red light; the colour was worked out from its light, not seen directly.
items.matters: The same study of 151 nearby white dwarfs found about one in 30 shines an unusual colour, such as pink.

items.title: UK regulator moves to give Microsoft special status in business software
items.why: Britain's Competition and Markets Authority proposed on 16 October to give Microsoft 'strategic market status' in business software, covering Word, Excel, Teams and its Copilot AI assistant. That would let it set rules on how Microsoft bundles products. A final decision is due by February; Microsoft says it disagrees.
items.matters: About 20 million people a month in Britain use this software; the CMA wants customers free to pick rival AI tools.

items.title: EU leaders back Zelensky as Trump calls Ukraine's refinery strikes 'disgrace'
items.why: At an EU summit in Brussels on Friday, Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky asked for an extra €70bn for next year and criticised a US deal to buy Russian diesel. EU leaders condemned the deal. US President Donald Trump called Ukraine's renewed strikes on Russian refineries a 'disgrace'.
items.matters: With ties between Kyiv and Washington strained, Europe is being asked to cover more of the cost of Ukraine's defence.

items.title: Four killed fighting fires as Indonesia faces worst blazes in a decade
items.why: Four members of a firefighting team died on Thursday when a blaze trapped them in Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park in East Java, Indonesia, officials say. Indonesia's foreign minister said President Prabowo Subianto has agreed to accept help from neighbouring countries to fight fires, mostly on Sumatra and Borneo.
items.matters: Smoke from the fires has spread haze to neighbouring countries, closing schools in Malaysia and East Timor.

items.changed: Updated: Champi became a typhoon and Guam moved to its highest alert
items.title: Typhoon Champi heads for Guam as island moves to highest alert
items.why: Champi became a typhoon on Saturday and is forecast to pass just south of Guam, in the western Pacific, on Sunday as a Category 3 storm. Guam's governor raised the island to its highest readiness level; the US weather service warns of severe damage and power cuts lasting days.
items.matters: It is the third powerful storm to threaten the Mariana Islands this year; some families still live in tents after earlier typhoons.

items.title: Milwaukee Brewers sweep Dodgers to reach first World Series since 1982
items.why: The Milwaukee Brewers came from 4-0 down to beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 6-4 in Los Angeles on Thursday night, winning the National League Championship Series 4-0. The two-time defending champions are out; the World Series starts in Milwaukee on 23 October.
items.matters: Milwaukee, Major League Baseball's smallest media market, is chasing the first championship in the club's history.

items.changed: Updated: two missiles hit Aden airport on Friday night; no casualties reported
items.title: Houthi missiles hit Aden's presidential palace, then its airport
items.why: Houthi missiles struck Yemen's presidential palace in Aden on Thursday; the health ministry says at least five people were killed and 16 injured. On Friday night, officials say, two more missiles hit Aden airport as a passenger plane prepared to leave. No casualties were reported.
items.matters: Aden is the seat of Yemen's internationally recognised government, as fighting between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia escalates.

items.title: Police clash with marchers in Buenos Aires over university funding
items.why: On Thursday, thousands of students and lecturers marched on Argentina's Congress in Buenos Aires, demanding President Javier Milei's government apply a university funding law. Police used tear gas and water cannon after some protesters threw stones. La Nación reports more than 30 people detained.
items.matters: The government says the law lacks funding; a University of Buenos Aires study says real funding fell about 40% since 2023.

items.title: ECB clears Italy's UniCredit to take control of Germany's Commerzbank
items.why: The European Central Bank has allowed UniCredit to raise its stake in Commerzbank above 30%, with no upper limit, UniCredit said on 15 October. It expects about 50% of the voting rights by the end of 2026. Germany's government, a Commerzbank shareholder, wants guarantees about its future.
items.matters: It would put one of Germany's biggest lenders to businesses under the control of a foreign bank.

items.title: Nearly half of reef-building coral species face higher extinction risk, study says
items.why: A peer-reviewed reassessment for the IUCN Red List, published in Nature on 15 October, found 340 of 774 assessed reef-building coral species (44%) threatened, up from about a third in 2008. The figure was first announced in 2024; lead author David Obura says ocean heat is the main cause.
items.matters: The data end in 2020, before the 2023–2025 global bleaching, so the authors say today's share is likely higher.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launch trailer reveals Justice as the game's composers
items.why: Rockstar Games released the launch trailer for Grand Theft Auto VI on 15 October and named French electronic duo Justice as composers of its score. The trailer features their new song with Tame Impala, SZA and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard; the game arrives on 19 November.
items.matters: The game's 34-track soundtrack album, out the same day, also features Travis Scott, Cardi B and Rauw Alejandro.

items.title: FIFA's Infantino apologises to council over investor plan; critics unsatisfied
items.why: FIFA president Gianni Infantino apologised to the FIFA Council in Zurich on 15 October for "mistakes" over a dropped $4.2 billion plan to sell a stake in World Cup commercial rights. European members, including England's Debbie Hewitt, said he gave no satisfactory answers.
items.matters: UEFA wants him replaced; rival candidates must be nominated by 18 November for FIFA's presidential election in Morocco in March.

items.title: Swedish parliament rejects Magdalena Andersson as prime minister
items.why: On Thursday, Sweden's parliament voted 248 to 99 against Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson becoming prime minister, a month after the 13 September election. Only her own party backed her, as the Left and Centre parties remain split over who should join a government.
items.matters: Parliament gets four attempts to approve a prime minister. If all four fail, Sweden must hold a snap election.

items.title: Jon Rahm agrees to leave LIV Golf, giving up remaining payments
items.why: Spanish golfer Jon Rahm has reached a separation agreement with LIV Golf, filed on 14 October in the league's bankruptcy case in New Jersey, USA. He drops all money claims, reportedly over $100 million, and his team stake; a judge must approve it on 5 November.
items.matters: LIV, in bankruptcy since September, loses one of its biggest names as it tries to relaunch in 2027.

items.title: World timekeepers vote to scrap the leap second from 2027
items.why: Delegates at the General Conference on Weights and Measures in Versailles, France, voted by majority on 15 October to stop adding leap seconds from 20 May 2027. Official time will instead be allowed to drift up to an hour from Earth's rotation.
items.matters: Leap seconds, 27 added since 1972, can disrupt computer systems; a 'leap hour' is not expected to be needed for centuries.

items.title: Amsterdam zoo hornbill gets 3D-printed upper and lower beak in reported first
items.why: A southern ground hornbill at Artis zoo in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, that broke both parts of its beak digging for food has been fitted with two 3D-printed prostheses by Utrecht vets and specialists. The zoo says it caught a mouse two days after surgery.
items.matters: Artis says it knows of no earlier case of a bird receiving both an upper and lower beak prosthesis.

items.title: Iranian film 'Midday Meal' wins top prize at Busan film festival
items.why: Majid Majidi's Midday Meal won Best Film at the 31st Busan International Film Festival in South Korea on 15 October, chosen from 13 Asian films by a jury led by China's Zhang Yimou. India's Birds in the Dark won the New Currents award for new directors.
items.matters: Under a new Academy rule, the win makes Midday Meal eligible for next year's Oscar for best international feature.

items.title: Australia edge New Zealand 24-22 in Rugby League World Cup opener
items.why: Australia beat New Zealand 24-22 at Sydney's Allianz Stadium on 15 October in the opening match of the Rugby League World Cup. Debutant Jack Bostock scored three tries, including the late winner, before a crowd of 41,255.

items.title: IMF raises sub-Saharan Africa growth forecast but warns of rising inflation
items.why: The International Monetary Fund now expects sub-Saharan Africa's economies to grow 4.5% in 2026, up from the 4.3% it forecast in April, it said on 15 October. It expects median inflation to rise to 4.3% this year and 5% in 2027, while aid to Africa falls a further 12%.
items.matters: The IMF says the region has little room to absorb another shock, such as renewed energy disruption or a strong El Niño.

items.title: UN report finds fewer than half of national nature targets on track
items.why: A UN assessment launched on 15 October in Yerevan, Armenia, found fewer than half of countries' biodiversity targets are on track. Current pledges would protect only 26% of land and 12% of the ocean by 2030, short of the 30% goal agreed in 2022.
items.matters: The findings frame the COP17 biodiversity talks, which run in Yerevan from 19 to 30 October.

items.changed: Updated: more heavy rain is forecast for Saturday on saturated ground
items.title: Istanbul's heaviest rain in over 80 years causes deadly floods
items.why: Flash floods hit Istanbul, Turkey's largest city, after record rain from Wednesday. Interior Minister Mustafa Çiftçi called it the worst flooding since 1942; at least four people have died, officials say. Turkey's weather service has warned of more heavy rain on Saturday on already saturated ground.
items.matters: Turkey's environment minister linked the floods to climate change weeks before Turkey hosts the COP31 UN climate summit.

items.changed: Updated: service partly restored; Reuters reports the order came from inside the White House
items.title: Ukraine says Starlink partly restored; sources say White House ordered limits
items.why: A Ukrainian Defence Ministry source says links on moving drones work again, but only up to about 160 km/h, after sudden cuts on 14 October. Two US officials told Reuters the order to slow it came from inside the White House; a senior US official denies Trump asked for it.
items.matters: Ukraine relies heavily on Starlink satellite internet for drones and frontline communications in its war with Russia.

items.changed: Updated: a third case, another relative, was confirmed
items.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case, a relative of the first patient
items.why: Kenya's health ministry confirmed a third Ebola case on 16 October: a 65-year-old woman, a close relative of the first two cases, who had been in quarantine since 6 October. The ministry says 127 of 130 contacts are in quarantine and there is no evidence of community spread.
items.matters: The cases are linked to Congo's outbreak, which has passed 9,000 cases; the Bundibugyo strain has no licensed vaccine.

items.changed: Updated: the Asian Tour has postponed its Riyadh season finale
items.title: Saudi golf and tennis events postponed following attacks on Riyadh
items.why: The Asian Tour on 15 October postponed its $5 million PIF Saudi International, due in Riyadh on 18–21 November, citing logistical challenges. The Six Kings Slam tennis exhibition has already moved to December. Saudi organisers say January's AFC Asian Cup remains on schedule.
items.matters: The disruption follows a 10 October strike on Riyadh's airport, claimed by Yemen's Houthis, that Reuters says killed 14 people.
